content_list.content_text: Carl Jung was fascinated by films. "The cinema, like the detective story," he observed, "makes it possible to experience without danger all the excitement, passion and desirousness which must be repressed in a humanitarian ordering of life." This is precisely the role of the psychological drama: to explore the inner worlds of the characters (and, by association, of the viewers).

information.contentText: Blue Velvet was originally the title of a song performed by Bobby Vinton. The song appears in the film and served as inspiration for its title. Roy Orbison's song "In Dreams" also plays a prominent role in the film.

content_list.content_text: Sometimes they gain understanding - House of Games (1987). In Sous le soleil de Satan (Under the Sun of Satan, 1987), for example, they are destroyed. In Sleuth (1972), the hero's curiosity, greed and envy bring about his downfall. Jeffrey's odyssey through the terrifying world of Blue Velvet (1986) feeds his own fascination: he is both attracted and repelled. This makes him at once protagonist and antagonist - and, in doing so, confirms that humanity really is its own worst enemy.

As Freud suggests, to understand ourselves we must confront our secret (and repressed) desires. Bernardo Bertolucci (b. 1940) drew on his fantasies about anonymous sex with a beautiful woman to create Ultimo tango a Parigi (Last Tango in Paris, 1972). The result is a meditation on grief, sexual violence and fantasy; the director gave outward form to his secret, unspoken thoughts.

information.contentText: Kubrick was a perfectionist who researched meticulously, with hundreds of photographs taken of potential locations, as well as of many scenes; however, according to Malcolm McDowell, he usually "got it right" early on, so there were few takes. So meticulous was Kubrick that McDowell stated: "If Kubrick hadn't been a film director he'd have been a General Chief of Staff of the US Forces. No matter what it is - even if it's a question of buying a shampoo it goes through him. He just likes total control." Filming took place between September 1970 and April 1971, making A Clockwork Orange the fastest shoot of his career. Technically, to achieve and convey the fantastical, dreamlike quality of the story, he shot with extreme wide-angle lenses such as the Kinoptik Tegea 9.8mm for 35mm Arriflex cameras, and used fast and slow motion to convey the mechanical nature of the bedroom sex scene or to stylize the violence in a manner similar to Toshio Matsumoto's Funeral Parade of Roses (1969).

content_list.content_text: In Il portiere di notte (The Night Porter, 1974), director Liliana Cavani (b. 1933) questions power, choice, guilt and sexual desire. A former SS officer is confronted with a figure from his past - a woman with whom he had a sadomasochistic affair while she was imprisoned in a concentration camp. For Freud, this is the very essence of repression - a secret history of sexual encounters and the ongoing struggle to deny or refute them. The Night Porter exposes the characters' deepest desires and asks the audience to confront their own.

quote.quote: The most brilliant suspense film ever made out of life in a small American town.
quote.author: Sheila Benson on Blue Velvet (1986)

content_list.content_text: In his theory of the "mirror stage" of human development, psychoanalyst Jacques Lacan examined the role of the mirror in allowing a small child to think of itself as an individual ("I") separate from its mother and the rest of the world. In films, the concept of the mirror image can be expressed metaphorically, by exploring the way antagonist and protagonist define each other. In Manhunter (1986), the hero gains crucial insight into the minds of killers by being able to think like them.

information.contentText: Don't Look Now focuses on the psychology of grief and the effect a child's death can have on a relationship; this portrayal of grief has been identified as unusually strong for a film with supernatural plot elements.

content_list.content_text: Hero and villain are like two halves - opposite but linked, like Blaney and Rusk in Frenzy (1972), by Alfred Hitchcock (1899-1980). In Blade Runner (1982), the protagonist Deckard understands the conflict of the antagonist, Batty. If we assume that Deckard, like Batty, is a replicant, they are, in effect, brothers. David Cronenberg (b. 1943) took this to the extreme in Dead Ringers (1988), in which twin brothers share each other's lives - one whole split in two - and one cannot exist without the other.

Psychological dramas plunge into the darkest places of the mind. Spoorloos (The Vanishing, 1988) is a terrifying study of the psyche of a killer, a family man who has lived a "good life" but whose inner and outer personalities are very different. In Don't Look Now (1973), a grieving couple travels to Venice shortly after the death of their daughter. The husband - who may have psychic gifts - is tormented by glimpses of a figure in a red coat, which reminds him of his daughter. The audience's understanding of events remains as limited and faltering as that of the husband and wife in their grief. In the words of David Mamet: "Viewers understand that they are the protagonists, and indeed, for one night they truly are, because the drama is their dream."

movies.title: Blue Velvet
movies.overview: The discovery of a severed human ear found in a field leads a young man on an investigation related to a beautiful, mysterious nightclub singer and a group of criminals who have kidnapped her child.

movies.title: A Clockwork Orange
movies.overview: In a near-future Britain, young Alexander DeLarge and his pals get their kicks beating and raping anyone they please. When not destroying the lives of others, Alex swoons to the music of Beethoven. The state, eager to crack down on juvenile crime, gives an incarcerated Alex the option to undergo an invasive procedure that'll rob him of all personal agency. In a time when conscience is a commodity, can Alex change his tune?

movies.title: Don't Look Now
movies.overview: Laura and John, grieved by a terrible loss, meet in Venice, where John is in charge of the restoration of a church, two mysterious sisters, one of whom gives them a message sent from the afterlife.

movies.title: The Night Porter
movies.overview: A concentration camp survivor discovers her former torturer and lover working as a porter at a hotel in postwar Vienna. When the couple attempt to re-create their sadomasochistic relationship, his former SS comrades begin to stalk them.

movies.title: Images
movies.overview: Schizophrenic housewife, engulfed by terrorizing apparitions, kills off each, unknowing if these demons are merely figments of her hallucinatory imagination or part of reality.

movies.title: Solaris
movies.overview: A psychologist is sent to a space station orbiting a planet called Solaris to investigate the death of a doctor and the mental problems of cosmonauts on the station. He soon discovers that the water on the planet is a type of brain which brings out repressed memories and obsessions.

movies.title: The Day of the Locust
movies.overview: Hollywood, 1930s. Tod Hackett, a young painter who tries to make his way as an art director in the lurid world of film industry, gets infatuated with his neighbor Faye Greener, an aspiring actress who prefers the life that Homer Simpson, a lone accountant, can offer her.

movies.title: The Stepford Wives
movies.overview: Joanna Eberhart has come to the quaint little town of Stepford, Connecticut with her family, but soon discovers there lies a sinister truth in the all too perfect behavior of the female residents.

movies.title: Altered States
movies.overview: A research scientist explores the boundaries and frontiers of consciousness. Using sensory deprivation and hallucinogenic mixtures from native American shamans, he explores these altered states of consciousness and finds that memory, time, and perhaps reality itself are states of mind.

content_list.title: Timeline of Events from 1970 to 1989
content_list.description: The Exorcist is released, making audiences around the world sick and causing them to faint, creating a global hysteria. The first blockbuster is released: Jaws; meanwhile, auteur cinema grows with Martin Scorsese and other great directors. The '80s arrive with low-budget productions and era-defining comedies.
